s5e1460976a73f9: Demo, for example, uses two typical AI workloads: YOLO access and Qwen3-8B large model reference missions. In the traditional Kubernetes Scheduling model, these types of tasks usually require exclusive GPU operations, while under the Hami Scheduling model, GPU is split into "compute resources + GPU memory" resource units that can be shared by multiple Pods on demand.
sb022831977592e: In the actual demonstration, several YOLO examples are being run by scheduling on the same GPU, while the Qwen3-8B model is co-located with other workloads through the binpack policy. Different types of AI workload coexist on the same GPU while keeping resources controlled.
sc473a3605b9ea0: This Demo presents not just an increase in the GPU utilization rate, but more importantly a new infrastructure capacity: the GPU is moving from "equipment" to "scheduling resources", and Kubernetes is having the basic ability to manage AI workload.
s91448d776e66eb: It's not a regular stand, or an overflowing technology sharing, but rather bringing HAMi into the wider global context on the main stage of concern for the mass population.
